---
title: "Initialise a table with `TABULATE`"
---

The `TABULATE` clause marks the beginning of a ggsql table declaration, like `VISUALISE` does for ggsql plots. 
As such it demarcates where the regular query ends and the table construction query starts. 
Everything that comes before the `TABULATE` clause is considered a standard SQL query that is sent to the backend. 
If that standard SQL ends with a `SELECT` query, this will automatically be added as the data for the table.

Currently, the only writer supporting the `TABULATE` clause is the HTML writer.

## Clause syntax
The `TABULATE` clause requires a column selection and optionally a data source.

```ggsql
TABULATE <column>, ... | * FROM <data-source>
```

## Column selection

```ggsql
<column>, ... | *
```

After `TABULATE` you can list columns separated by commas to display in the table.
The order in which you select columns affects the display-order in the output.
The columns can be selected in (a mixture of) one of three forms:

* `<column>` reuses the column name as header label
* `<column> AS <label>` sets a new name for a column
* `*` selects all (remaining) columns, in the source's order

Without the `*` wildcard, only the listed columns are kept.
The wildcard can be combined with explicit columns to partially order columns.
When a column is renamed using the `AS` keyword, other table clauses --- like `LABEL`, `SPAN` and `FORMAT` --- use the *new* name.
It is discouraged to name column `title`, `subtitle` or `captions` as these are keywords in the [`LABEL`](label-tabulate.qmd) clause.

```ggsql
-- Select all columns
TABULATE *

-- Select 3 specific columns
TABULATE foo, bar, baz

-- Renaming columns
TABULATE foo AS "Foo Label", bar AS "Bar Label"

-- Fix position of first and last columns
TABULATE foo, *, baz
```

## Data source

```ggsql
FROM <data-source>
```

The `TABULATE` clause can have a `FROM` clause that defines the source of the data.
Alternatively data can be implied from any terminal `SELECT` clause in the preceding SQL query.
Having both a terminal `SELECT` clause and using `FROM` is an error.
The data received via `FROM` can take two forms:

* Bare **Table** or **CTE** that is available in the backend, either as CTE defined in the preceding SQL query or as a proper table in the database.
* A **File path** as (single quoted) string, that points to a file that can be read by the backend.

```ggsql
-- Use table as data source
TABULATE * FROM my_table

-- Use file as data source
TABULATE * FROM 'my_dataset.csv'

-- With preceding SQL
SELECT foo, bar, baz FROM my_table
TABULATE *
```

## Examples

Plain table from data

```{ggsql}
CREATE TEMP TABLE my_data AS SELECT * FROM ggsql:penguins LIMIT 5

TABULATE * FROM my_data
```

Reordering columns

```{ggsql}
TABULATE island, *, species FROM my_data
```

Renaming columns on the fly. For order-preserving renames, see [`LABEL`](label-tabulate.qmd) clause.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE 
  bill_len AS "Bill Length",  
  bill_dep AS "Bill Depth",
  *
  FROM my_data
```
